method: scripts/bench-engine.py: 10 fresh processes, spawn to first hello response (median and max); size of the unpacked one-dir folder or of the one-file binary; peak RSS of the process tree (ru_maxrss; not measured on Windows). The release asset is the one-dir folder packed as .tar.gz (.zip on Windows), 9.5 to 10.7 MB.
decision: one-dir. On the local macOS arm64 machine one-file starts in about 4 s (it unpacks itself on every start and macOS scans each new executable), far over the 1 s target, while one-dir starts in 0.13 s. On the GitHub runners one-file is also slower than one-dir (macos-x64: 0.96 s against 0.69 s, windows: 0.71 s against 0.33 s) and only 0.04 to 0.09 s slower on Linux, so one-dir is the format that meets the cold-start target on every platform with margin. Its cost is size: 39.0 MB (macos-arm64) and 39.6 MB (macos-x64) unpacked, under the 40 MB target with almost no margin (the macOS Python framework ships twice); Linux and Windows are about 22 MB. Nuitka was not measured: PyInstaller one-dir meets both targets on all five platforms.

macos-arm64-local.machine: Apple M-series, 12 cores, macOS 26 (Darwin 25.5), measured locally
